topic: Air Pressure, Wind, and Tropical Cyclones
key_concepts: Wind blows because of differences in air pressure.
Air is a mixture of gases whose weight creates air pressure.
Temperature differences create differences in air pressure.
Heated air particles move quickly, spread out, and rise.
Low pressure areas contain fewer air particles than high pressure areas.
Air moves from high-pressure areas to low-pressure areas.
A greater air pressure difference produces stronger wind.
Tropical cyclones are violent weather systems with strong winds and heavy rain.
Tropical cyclones form over warm oceans where rising air creates a low pressure area.
Tropical cyclones are named typhoon, hurricane, or cyclone depending on location.
